rows.description: A toddler among weeping adults clings and looks worried, sensing tension without understanding. Simple presence and holding calm the child, while excluding them entirely can frighten more.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, grief, fear, anxiety

rows.description: A parent tells a child grandpa's body stopped working and he will not come back, without euphemisms like sleeping. Plain words reduce fear, and repeated questions are normal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child whose friend lost a parent sits beside them and offers a toy or asks to play. Presence and ordinary activities often comfort more than words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager tells a grieving friend at least he lived long or everything happens for a reason. Well-meant phrases often hurt, and I am so sorry and I am here work better.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult brings food, sits at the funeral house and lets the bereaved talk or stay silent. Regular small contact in the weeks after, when others fade, counts most.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A bereaved person insists they are fine, afraid of burdening others, while feeling numb or angry. Many find relief when someone asks about the person they lost by name.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: grief, anger, fear, relief

rows.description: An angry child kicks and screams, needing help to calm before any talk can happen. A calm adult who stays nearby and names the feeling later teaches regulation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child hearing a parent shout freezes, shrinks or argues. Fear blocks understanding, and a later calm conversation is when the lesson can actually land.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anger, fear, calm

rows.description: A teenager facing a friend who is furious does not argue or explain first and lets them vent, then says I can see you are really upset. Listening first lowers the heat and allows a real talk.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A professional faces an angry client, keeps voice low, acknowledges the frustration, and asks what outcome would help. Angry people often need to feel heard before they can problem-solve.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17
